sources.title: Fowler and Sadalage: evolutionary database design
sources.supportRationale: Versioned schema changes and compatible transition periods.

sources.title: Danilo Sato: Parallel Change
sources.supportRationale: Expand, migrate and contract pattern; no universal rollback guarantee.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: ALTER TABLE
sources.supportRationale: Locking, constraint validation and schema-change conditions.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: explicit locking
sources.supportRationale: Row locks, lock lifetimes and deadlock prevention.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: transactions
sources.supportRationale: Explicit transaction boundaries and commit/rollback behavior.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: CREATE INDEX
sources.supportRationale: Concurrent builds, failure states and transaction restrictions.

sources.title: AWS Builders Library: making retries safe with idempotent APIs
sources.supportRationale: Stable request identity and semantic duplicate handling for uncertain outcomes.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: continuous archiving and recovery
sources.supportRationale: Independent base backups, WAL archives and point-in-time recovery.

scenarios.theme: Old pods still use the old name during a column rename. What release sequence will you choose?
scenarios.assumptions: A live service wants display_name renamed to full_name while old and new versions overlap. Immediate rename breaks old readers/writers. What will you do?

scenarios.theme: A phased constraint migration still blocks writes for a long time. Which transaction boundary matters?

scenarios.theme: A restarted backfill overwrites live edits and skips locked rows. How will you make it safe?

scenarios.theme: The migration fails because concurrent index creation runs inside a transaction. How will deployment recover?
scenarios.assumptions: A release uses a PostgreSQL concurrent index build to reduce write blocking, but its migration runner wraps every step atomically. A failed attempt may also leave an invalid index. What will you change?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

scenarios.theme: Old and new databases diverge during a migration. Can the request simply retry both writes?
scenarios.assumptions: A migration writes each business change to two independent databases. A crash after the first commit leaves one copy stale, and deletes/retries can reorder. How will you establish a trustworthy transition?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.
